description: Hair standing on end, the heart melting, tears of joy, faltering voice, weeping, laughing, singing aloud without shame and dancing as signs of devotion that purifies the world.
Singing the beloved's names, love born and heart melted, one laughs, weeps, cries, sings and dances like one mad, beyond the world.
Prahlāda weeping, laughing, singing, crying out, dancing, imitating the Lord, and sitting silent with hair on end and tearful half-closed eyes.
In separation the gopīs, absorbed in Kṛṣṇa, imitate his deeds and identify with him (tanmayatā).
Melting love, then release of the image; the mind without support suddenly goes out like a flame; the self seen as one without division; the body no longer noticed.
The composed meditator sees the Lord as the self in the self, 'light joined with light'.
First signs of yoga: lightness, health, gentleness, pleasant smell, scant excreta, radiance, clarity, pleasant voice; affection of others, fearlessness of creatures, indifference to heat and cold.
Prātibha (all learning shines forth), śrāvaṇa (hearing from a thousand yojanas), daiva (godlike sight), bhrama (unsupported wandering of mind), āvarta (knowledge whirling like a whirlpool).
stage: after the self has been seen

description: In the seven subtle dhāraṇās the yogin experiences himself as the subtle earth (losing smell), then water, fire, air, space, mind and intellect, abandoning each.
Pratibhā (knowing the subtle, hidden, past, distant and future), śravaṇa (hearing all sounds), vārtā, darśana (divine sights), āsvāda (divine tastes), vedanā (divine touch).
In the higher grades of prāṇāyāma: sweat and trembling, then bliss, horripilation, tears, babbling, whirling and swooning.
Śānti (calamities calmed), praśānti (darkness within and without destroyed), dīpti (light within and without), prasāda (clarity of the intellect).
The eighteen (plus five) powers such as becoming minute or vast, hearing and seeing at a distance, entering another's body, dying at will, knowing others' minds.
Not seeing the path of the gods, the pole-star, Venus, the moon's shadow or Arundhatī: death within a year; further signs with shorter spans.
The pain of death like countless scorpion stings, failing senses and consciousness, frothing at the mouth; the thumb-sized person leaves crying 'alas' and looks back at home.
Sinners see Yama with fanged, frowning face amid diseases; the virtuous see him gentle, crowned and radiant.
Mārkaṇḍeya's vision of the deluge and the infant on the banyan leaf, within whose body he saw the whole universe.
